entries.headline: Weekly flu toll hits five-year high: 219 severe cases, 44 deaths
entries.why: Multiple outlets carried the record severity figures over three days, and doctors tied them to vaccination appeals for older and chronically ill people. This is now the dominant frame for all flu coverage.

entries.headline: Public flu uptake reaches 1.91 million in eight days; official voices supply worry
entries.why: Reports quote Lo Yi-chun worrying that supply may not be enough, against 7.05 million doses procured. Supply adequacy is likely to become a political and media question if demand holds.

entries.headline: Taiwan CDC: uptake strong, severe cases mostly unvaccinated older adults
entries.zh: 公費流感及新冠疫苗接種踴躍 請符合資格民眾儘速接種 及早獲得保護力
entries.why: The CDC's latest notice frames severity around unvaccinated older adults and urges vaccination before holiday travel. This sets the official message that local bureaus and doctors are amplifying.

entries.headline: Posts report self-pay flu stock delays to November and NT$1,950 prices
entries.why: Users report Kaohsiung clinics without self-pay stock until November and complain about cost, while others report limited brand choice for public doses. Thin but high-engagement signal of access friction outside the public programme.

entries.headline: Paediatric flu dosing rule change and nasal-spray fever posts confuse parents
entries.why: Media report children 6 months to 3 years now need two doses this year, and parents post conflicting clinic answers and fever worries about nasal spray. Clarity on paediatric schedules is an emerging issue.

entries.headline: Clinic post promotes adjuvanted flu vaccine with unverified comparative protection claims
entries.why: A clinic's Threads post claims 20-30% better protection and 12-month duration and invites bookings; it is flagged as misleading. Comparative claims around enhanced vaccines are a compliance and reputational sensitivity.

watch.text: Planned start of 150,000 Novavax COVID doses alongside the joint flu and COVID programme.
Whether self-pay flu stock arrives at clinics as posts report, and whether flu activity eases as media forecast.
Whether severe-case and death counts stay at five-year highs and whether officials repeat supply concerns.

qa.q: Is there an official flu vaccine shortage?
qa.a: No official shortage notice in the digest. CDC procured 7.05 million doses (about 6.449 million standard and 170,000 enhanced); 1.91 million were given in eight days and an official said supply may not suffice. Social posts report self-pay stock delays in Kaohsiung.

Low-level only. A side-effect diary post and parents' nasal-spray fever posts drew engagement, PTS reported a first vaccine relief award for leg paralysis, and two low-engagement posts making misleading safety claims were flagged. Mainstream media coverage remains pro-vaccination.

qa.q: Anything on RSV, Tdap or high-dose flu?
qa.a: Very little. RSV volume rose from 0 to 7 items, led by a Threads post summarising a European maternal RSV vaccine study; Tdap had 5 items, mainly via chronic lung disease recommendations; high-dose flu had zero items. Enhanced-type coverage fell from 18 to 12.

policy_notes.why: Sets the 2026 programme baseline: phase 1 for 11 groups from October 1 with about 6.449 million standard and 170,000 enhanced doses plus health-coin incentives.
Launch event confirmed 7.05 million flu doses procured including enhanced vaccine, the figure now used to judge supply adequacy.
CDC links ongoing severe flu activity to unvaccinated older adults and urges pre-holiday vaccination, framing the current severity narrative.

misinfo.claim: Adjuvanted Japanese flu vaccine gives 20-30% more protection than standard vaccines and lasts 12 months
misinfo.note: Clinic promotional claim for a prescription vaccine; track spread and advertising-compliance angle, keep any company comment to approved label information, no amplification.

misinfo.claim: Vaccines contain viral particles and community calls to vaccinate over-65s endanger elders
misinfo.note: Single low-engagement post; monitor only, existing CDC and medical myth-busting content is sufficient.

misinfo.claim: Receiving flu and COVID shots together is untested and the campaign is electioneering
misinfo.note: Zero-engagement comment; monitor for co-administration safety and liability questions recurring as uptake grows.

products.name: Beyfortus
products.signal: Nothing in the digest mentions nirsevimab or infant antibodies. RSV volume rose from 0 to 7, driven by one Threads post summarising a European maternal RSV vaccination study, plus COPD/asthma coverage that names RSV vaccines.
products.implication: Infant RSV prevention is entering public conversation through the maternal-vaccine route, and parents are being directed to obstetricians. No policy or media signal on infant antibodies yet.
products.action: Monitor. Prepare a neutral, evidence-based briefing on the infant RSV burden and the prevention options available in Taiwan, for use only in stakeholder dialogue. Map obstetric and paediatric society contacts ahead of any season-planning discussions.

products.name: High-dose influenza vaccine
products.sub: older adults; no high-dose-specific items this week
products.signal: Zero high-dose items this week. The adjacent 'enhanced' category is active: the CDC procured about 170,000 enhanced doses within about 7.05 million total, and doctors urge high-risk older adults toward enhanced vaccine. Some media and clinic posts cite comparative protection figures, and one clinic adjuvanted claim is flagged as misleading.
products.implication: Record severe cases concentrated in unvaccinated older adults are strengthening the older-adult policy case. However, limited enhanced supply, combined with comparative claims circulating outside official channels, raises access-equity and advertising-compliance sensitivities for any product in this space.
products.action: Issue readiness: prepare factual supply and access lines for questions from officials and clinicians. Compile older-adult burden evidence from this season for next-season policy dialogue with the CDC. Remind partners and clinics of advertising restrictions on prescription vaccines.

products.name: Tdap booster
products.signal: Tdap volume rose from 0 to 5, but none of these items appears in the top items provided. The only visible context is storyline labels on vaccine recommendations for chronic lung disease and COPD/asthma patients.
products.implication: Signal is too thin to characterise. Pertussis appears only as part of a broader respiratory-vaccine bundle for chronic lung patients.
products.action: Monitor and pull the underlying items before drawing conclusions. Note respiratory and chest physicians as a possible venue for future evidence-sharing on adult immunisation.

issues.title: Public flu vaccine supply strain and clinic stock-outs
issues.note: An official has voiced concern about sufficiency amid 1.9 million+ doses in eight days, and posts report limited brands and self-pay stock delayed to November (01e330c1cc59a5cb, 9d7586e562a1a9e4, d1ba3db7060af840, 518a82dbe192d5f6). Have factual supply and allocation lines ready.

issues.title: Comparative protection claims by clinics and media
issues.note: A clinic post with booking invitations cites 20-30% better protection for an adjuvanted vaccine, and media cite an enhanced-type 25% figure (3b39dfe939b73f54, ea6eca5155353258). This could draw scrutiny under prescription-medicine advertising rules, so keep company channels claim-free.

issues.title: Safety and co-administration narratives as programme widens
issues.note: Side-effect diaries draw high engagement, a first injury relief payout made the news, and posts question two-shot co-administration and liability (cd78d2dfe4e9e25d, d9b85a48502dc447, 9b2921169f62f87d). Novavax doses are planned for late October (4639c45b02b3796c); prepare to engage clinicians on co-administration questions.
